deploy-bot: Scheduled release 'service-api@v2.3.1-rc4' is queued for 2025-11-12T23:00:00Z. Initiating preflight checks. :gear:
Alice R.: Heads-up — we have an active incident (INC-4821) impacting DB failovers. Hold this release for now. Do not deploy. :warning:
Jamal (oncall): Confirming — incident started at 1750000200, cluster failovers unstable. Agree to hold.
Priya: Thanks. Quick ask: is the release safe to pin and reschedule, or do we need a rollback if it went out?
Max: No deploy happened yet per pipeline logs. Preflight blocked at canary validation. We should pin the current candidate and reschedule next change window.
Ravi: Product + PMs need ETA for reschedule so we can update stakeholders. Prefer earliest stable window.
Alice R.: Plan: 1) Mark release as ON_HOLD and pin candidate to tag `v2.3.1-rc4-pending` 2) Cancel active change window 3) Reschedule to next approved window (2025-11-13T03:00:00Z) pending incident closure 4) Post release notes update
Jamal (oncall): I'm creating a short incident note for the release doc. Also let's add a rollback play in case the release accidentally goes through.
Alice R.: Good call. Rollback snippet saved to the release ticket: ```bash
# rollback to last stable
cli deploy rollback --service service-api --to-tag v2.3.0-stable --reason "INC-4821 hold"
```
Priya: Also pin runtime dependencies in the release config: `runtime.image: quay/redwood/service-api:v2.3.1-rc4-pending` so auto-rollouts won't pick newer hashes.
Max: I'll add a temporary gating rule in the orchestration plane to block this tag from being promoted until we remove the ON_HOLD label. Means even if CI thinks it's green, deploy will be blocked.
Ravi: For release notes, add a short blurb: "Deployment held due to database failover incident; rescheduling pending stability checks." We'll send a customer-facing note if windows are impacted.
Alice R.: Action items assigned: Jamal — update INC-4821 with timeline and note about release hold. Max — implement orchestration gate. Priya — confirm pin applied in repo. Ravi — draft stakeholder comms. I'll update the release ticket and unhold when we have green from SRE.
deploy-bot: Release 'service-api@v2.3.1-rc4' status changed to ON_HOLD by Alice R. (reason: incident-triggered hold INC-4821).
Jamal (oncall): Quick Q — if incident persists past the next window, do we move to a maintenance window next week or try canary-only?
Priya: If incident lingers, we prefer to delay full rollout and consider canary-only in a different cluster that isn't affected. That requires validation from Max and network config review.
Max: Canary-only on an isolated cluster is feasible but needs a short runbook update — I can prepare it if needed. For now, target reschedule to 2025-11-13T03:00:00Z and we'll reassess 2 hours before.
Alice R.: Agreed. I'll set the change window in the calendar and put a reminder 2h prior. Also creating a follow-up ticket to capture lessons learned and to add an automatic release-hold trigger on incident severity >= S2 in future.
Ravi: Thanks everyone. Please add any dependencies to the release ticket. I'll hold off on external comms until we confirm the new time. :+1:
deploy-bot: Reminder set: Change window 2025-11-13T03:00:00Z (reschedule tentative) — will post update 2 hours before.
Alice R.: Closing thread. Reopen if anything changes.
